newsitem.title: ITALY: Woody Allen presents new film for Venice theatre.
newsitem.headline: Woody Allen presents new film for Venice theatre.

text.p: Film director Woody Allen brought his latest movie to Venice on Tuesday to raise money for the city's fire-ravaged opera house but said he planned to slip away before the show started.
"I don't see my own movies after I finish them," Allen told reporters before the European premiere of his musical "Everyone Says I Love You" in the elegant Italian lagoon city.

The American director told a news conference overlooking the Grand Canal he planned to go to the Palazzo del Cinema at the Venice Lido to greet moviegoers but that he did not like seeing himself in the cinema.
"So I would like to say hello and let the audience see the movie and I'll go maybe to a restaurant or take walk on the beach and when it's over come back and say thank you," Allen said.

The film, Allen's first attempt at a musical, has a star-spangled cast including Alan Alda, Goldie Hawn, Julia Roberts as well as Allen himself. It uses songs by Cole Porter and Richard Rodgers and Lorenz Hart.
Allen became involved with fundraising for Venice's 18th century Fenice opera house soon after it was gutted last January in a fire now suspected to have been arson.
He had been due to play there on a tour of his New Orleans Jazz Band but was forced to shift the performance to a nearby venue. He donated the proceeds to the Fenice's reconstruction.
Proceeds from the film premiere -- tickets cost 30,000 lire ($19) each -- will also go towards rebuilding the theatre. That is expected to cost 120 billion lire and take until November 1999.
"I've been trying to do something for the Fenice since I was last here in Venice and I'm only glad that my picture is ready now," Allen told Reuters Television.

"Everyone Says I Love You" is set in modern New York, Paris and Venice and follows the amorous exploits of a wealthy New York family, headed by Alda and Hawn. Allen features as Hawn's luckless ex-husband and father of one of her daughters.
Allen apologised to reporters for his singing in the film.
"At home I sing fearlessly in the shower. I once thought years ago if I could give a concert at Carnegie Hall with the shower it would be perfect," he said.

He said he wanted to make a musical "for people who couldn't sing or dance... The important theme was always the emotional feeling. I didn't want performance trained voices which would be all technique and no feeling".

Allen, in Venice with his companion Soon Yi Previn, said he wanted to do more for the Fenice reconstruction project and had been asked to direct a fund-raising opera. He said the idea appealed to him but "I have never directed anything live in my life".

The Fenice, now shrouded in scaffolding and roofless, was opened in 1792 and burned down in 1836. It rose from the ashes of that fire like the mythical phoenix after which it is named and staged many Verdi operas in the 19th century. ($1=1,528 lire)
